subject: Quantitech — eligibility check + commercial exception request
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantitech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quantitech.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Potential pilot — request for pricing & compliance path

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking the call this morning. Quantitech is interested in a 6-week pilot of Redwood for an internal MRO (maintenance, repair, and overhaul) workflow we’re developing. A few important constraints on our side:

- We operate in the aerospace supply chain and have ITAR/controlled-technology exposure for a subset of data.
- Procurement needs a written confirmation of what controls/contractual language Redwood requires for restricted-technology customers (export control, permitted geos, data handling).
- We’re on a compressed timeline and would like to start the pilot in early December.

We’re also requesting a 30% pilot discount and a one-time exception to the standard DPA: specifically a clause allowing CO-located on-prem routing for sensitive workloads (we can share a proposed redline). Attached is our internal request form and an initial compliance questionnaire.

Attachments: Quantitech_Request_Form.docx, ComplianceQuestionnaire.xlsx

Can you advise next steps and whether Redwood can support the commercial exception + export control requirements for a pilot?

—Sanjay
Head of Digital Product, Quantitech

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantitech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Potential pilot — request for pricing & compliance path

Sanjay — thanks, this is helpful. I’ve attached the draft SOW we typically use for pilots and copied Deal Desk and Legal to start eligibility and redline review.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Deal Desk / Legal: confirm whether Quantitech’s aerospace exposure requires an export-control exception or a denial per policy.
2) Security: run the compliance questionnaire and identify gating items (KYC, sanctions screening, access controls).
3) Commercial: I’ll log a request for a one-time pilot discount (30%) and an exception to the DPA; Deal Desk to advise what level of executive sign-off we need.

If we can get risk sign-off by Friday (20th) we can hit a first-week-of-December start.

Attachments: SOW_Quantitech_Draft.pdf

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Monica / Laura —

Quick intake from Deal Desk: Quantitech looks like a mid-market opportunity but the aerospace exposure triggers our export-control review. We need Legal and Security to confirm whether the required change (on-prem routing allowance in DPA) is permissible.

From a commercial perspective: a 30% pilot discount is above our standard pilot band. I can approve up to 15% at the deal desk level; anything beyond requires VP/Sales approval + explicit risk acceptance from Security/Legal. Please escalate with a short exec summary.

Required items for escalation:
- Completed ComplianceQuestionnaire.xlsx (they attached but we need answers filled).
- Sanctions/KYC pass for the entity and key stakeholders.
- Proposed DPA redline (we need the exact wording).

I’ll add the deal to HubSpot and flag for a priority review (DEAL-2026-1042).

Rishi
Deal Desk Manager

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Potential pilot — request for pricing & compliance path

Monica —

Read through their questionnaire and the draft SOW. A few legal points:
- "On-prem routing" needs definition. If they mean customer-managed private routing inside their VPC (Redwood Private), that’s a supported pattern but requires a Private deployment contract and separate SOC/audit terms.
- If they want Redwood-hosted capability to process ITAR data without a Private deployment, that increases legal/regulatory risk and likely cannot be approved.
- Redline: I need their proposed DPA language. We should offer a scoped (pilot-only) addendum instead of changing the enterprise DPA. That addendum will limit exposure and expire after the pilot.

Can we get: the completed questionnaire with names of where controlled data will originate, and the exact DPA redline? Copying Security for the sanctions/KYC check.

Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 07:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Potential pilot — request for pricing & compliance path

Team —

I ran an initial sanctions and sanctions-screening check on Quantitech (entity & directors). No immediate hits on EU/US sanctions lists, but a secondary supplier they reference (AeroParts Global) appears on a denied party list in a non-US jurisdiction. Need deeper diligence:

- Confirm which data fields/workloads would be ITAR-controlled. If any controlled technical data is leaving their controlled on-prem env, that’s a hard stop without Private deployment.
- Recommend conditional approval path: approve pilot only if (a) pilot is in Redwood Private or customer-managed VPC routing, (b) we implement a strict list of allowed IPs, and (c) we collect KYC docs for beneficial owners.

I’ll prepare a short security risk memo for the execs. If Deal Desk wants 30% discount, Security will insist on a limited-term addendum and stronger indemnities.

Mina
Head of Security & Compliance

Thanks for the intake. My view: we can approve a pilot commercial exception but with clear guardrails. Approvals:

- Commercial: one-time 25% pilot discount (not 30%) with a clause that full production pricing will be standard rate.
- Legal/Security: require the scoped pilot addendum Laura suggested + Security memo sign-off.
- Term: pilot limited to 45 days and automatically terminates unless commercial expansion executed.

Rishi — please prepare the executive memo summarizing the residual risk and recommended discount. Laura/Mina — would like your sign-off by EOD Tuesday so Monica can respond to Quantitech.

Markus
VP, Sales

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed internally. We can move forward with a scoped pilot under the following conditions: 

- Pilot will run in Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC routing) or equivalent customer-hosted environment — Redwood will not process controlled ITAR data on our hosted shared environment for this pilot.
- Pilot term: up to 45 days, limited to the use cases in the attached SOW.
- Commercial: one-time 25% pilot discount approved. Any production expansion will revert to standard pricing.
- Contract: we will provide a Pilot Addendum (time-limited) instead of changing our standard DPA. Security & Legal must complete sign-off prior to start.

Next steps for Quantitech: please return the completed ComplianceQuestionnaire.xlsx with explicit fields called out as ITAR/controlled, and upload the proposed DPA redline. Once received, Legal/Security will complete final sign-off and I’ll send the addendum + DocuSign link.

Attachments: SOW_Quantitech_Draft.pdf

If this works, I’ll have our DocuSign link ready by close of business tomorrow.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
